title: Trying to Describe Computing (Classical vs Quantum)
full_prompt: Create a Manim scene using ManimGL/InteractiveScene that visualizes the concept of classical computing. The scene should feature two PiCreatures: Randolph (blue, on the left) and Buddy (maroon, on the right). Initially, display a 3D-rotated laptop in the center-top. Randolph points to the laptop while Buddy looks at it. Next, introduce a classical computer chip symbol (a computer chip SVG with a math symbol inside, e.g., '\mathcal{C}') and shift the laptop upwards. Then, display a factoring equation: '91 = 7 x 13'. Animate the numbers '7' and '7 x 13' moving into the chip, transforming into '91' to represent classical computation (multiplication/factoring). Finally, display a complex logic gate diagram (using an SVG like 'Four_bit_adder_with_carry_lookahead') with a stroke animation while the PiCreatures react to it.

common_failure_modes.note: The code relies on external SVG assets. If these are missing, SVGMobject will fail to load.

common_failure_modes.pattern: Use of custom PiCreature classes and methods in standard Manim Community
common_failure_modes.note: Randolph, PiCreature, and Blink are custom 3b1b classes and will not work in standard Manim Community without importing the active_projects/3b1b library.
InteractiveScene is specific to ManimGL and is not available in Manim Community.
